title: Life in the Extreme: Unveiling the Strange Wonders of the Deep Ocean
title_zh: 极端生命：揭秘深海的奇异景象
intro_zh: 本文约900词，介绍深海生物的奇特适应方式，包括生物发光、透明躯体、巨大化及热液喷口生态系统。适合CET-4水平，含6个核心生词。

paragraphs.en: The deep ocean, starting at about 200 meters below the surface, is a realm of total darkness, crushing pressure, and near-freezing temperatures. For centuries, humans thought this environment could not support life. However, modern deep-sea exploration has revealed a world teeming with bizarre creatures that have evolved incredible adaptations to survive. From glowing fish to transparent jellyfish, these organisms challenge our understanding of what it means to be alive.
paragraphs.zh: 深海，从海面下约200米开始，是一个完全黑暗、压力巨大、接近冰点的领域。几个世纪以来，人类认为这种环境无法维持生命。然而，现代深海探索揭示了一个充满奇异生物的世界，它们进化出了难以置信的适应能力以生存。从发光的鱼到透明的水母，这些生物挑战着我们对生命意义的理解。

paragraphs.en: One of the most common and fascinating features of deep-sea animals is bioluminescence — the ability to produce light through chemical reactions in their bodies. About 90% of deep-sea creatures can create light. They use it for various purposes: to attract mates, lure prey, confuse predators, or communicate. For example, the deep-sea anglerfish has a glowing lure on its head that dangles in front of its mouth. Small fish are attracted to the light, and when they get close, the anglerfish snaps them up.
paragraphs.zh: 深海动物最常见且最迷人的特征之一是生物发光——通过体内化学反应产生光的能力。约90%的深海生物能发光。它们利用这种能力达到多种目的：吸引配偶、引诱猎物、迷惑捕食者或交流。例如，深海鮟鱇鱼头部有一个发光的诱饵，在嘴前晃动。小鱼被光吸引，当它们靠近时，鮟鱇鱼就一口吞下。

paragraphs.en: Another strange survival strategy is transparency. Many deep-sea creatures, such as certain jellyfish and squid, have bodies so clear that they are nearly invisible. This helps them avoid predators in the dark water where there is no place to hide. One extreme example is the glass octopus, whose body is almost completely transparent except for its eyes and digestive organs. It can drift through the water undetected.
paragraphs.zh: 另一种奇特的生存策略是透明。许多深海生物，如某些水母和鱿鱼，身体极其透明，几乎看不见。这有助于它们在无处可藏的黑暗海水中躲避捕食者。一个极端的例子是玻璃章鱼，它的身体除了眼睛和消化器官外几乎完全透明，可以在水中不受察觉地漂流。

paragraphs.en: The deep sea also produces creatures of tremendous size. The giant squid, which can reach lengths of up to 13 meters, is a legendary inhabitant of the deep. For a long time, it was only known from dead specimens washed ashore. In 2004, Japanese scientists managed to photograph a live giant squid in its natural habitat for the first time. Such large size may help these animals travel long distances in search of food or mates in the vast, food-scarce ocean.
paragraphs.zh: 深海也孕育了体型巨大的生物。巨乌贼体长可达13米，是深海的传奇居民。很长一段时间里，人们只能从冲上岸的死亡标本中了解它。2004年，日本科学家首次在自然栖息地拍摄到活的巨乌贼。如此巨大的体型可能有助于这些动物在广阔、食物匮乏的海洋中长距离迁徙寻找食物或配偶。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most incredible deep-sea ecosystems are the hydrothermal vents. These are cracks in the ocean floor where superheated water, rich in minerals, erupts from below. The water can reach over 400°C, but the extreme pressure keeps it from boiling. Around these vents, entire communities of life thrive without sunlight. Bacteria use chemicals from the vents to produce energy through chemosynthesis, and in turn feed clams, shrimp, tube worms, and other organisms. Some tube worms can grow to over 2 meters long.
paragraphs.zh: 也许最不可思议的深海生态系统是热液喷口。这些是海底的裂缝，富含矿物质的超热水从中喷出。水温可超过400°C，但极高的压力阻止了沸腾。在这些喷口周围，整个生物群落无需阳光就能繁衍生息。细菌利用喷口中的化学物质通过化学合成产生能量，进而养活蛤、虾、管虫等生物。有些管虫可长到2米以上。

paragraphs.en: Despite the hostile conditions, deep-sea creatures have also evolved an amazing ability to withstand pressure. At depths of 4,000 meters, the pressure is about 400 times greater than at the surface. The bodies of deep-sea fish lack swim bladders (which would collapse), and their cells contain special proteins and molecules that keep their structures stable under high pressure. Some species, like the snailfish, have been found at depths of over 8,000 meters, making them the deepest-dwelling fish known.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管环境恶劣，深海生物还进化出了惊人的抗压能力。在4000米深处，压力是海面的约400倍。深海鱼类的身体没有鳔（否则会塌陷），它们的细胞含有特殊的蛋白质和分子，能在高压下保持结构稳定。有些物种如狮子鱼，曾在8000多米深处被发现，成为已知栖息最深的鱼类。

paragraphs.en: In recent years, deep-sea mining and fishing have threatened these unique ecosystems. The ocean floor contains valuable metals like manganese and cobalt, and companies want to extract them. However, scientists warn that disturbing these habitats could destroy species we haven't even discovered yet. Understanding and protecting the deep ocean is becoming increasingly urgent. After all, we know more about the surface of Mars than about the deepest parts of our own planet.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，深海采矿和捕捞威胁着这些独特的生态系统。海底含有锰、钴等贵重金属，公司希望开采它们。然而，科学家警告，干扰这些栖息地可能会摧毁我们尚未发现的物种。了解和保护深海变得越来越紧迫。毕竟，我们对火星表面的了解超过了对地球最深处的了解。

paragraphs.en: In conclusion, the deep ocean is a testament to life's ability to adapt to the most extreme conditions. From bioluminescent lures to transparent bodies, from giant squid to heat-loving tube worms, these creatures remind us that there are still countless wonders waiting to be discovered beneath the waves. As technology advances, we will continue to unveil the secrets of this dark, mysterious world.
paragraphs.zh: 总之，深海证明了生命适应极端条件的能力。从生物发光诱饵到透明身体，从巨乌贼到嗜热管虫，这些生物提醒我们，海浪之下仍有无数奇观等待发现。随着技术进步，我们将继续揭示这个黑暗神秘世界的秘密。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of bioluminescence in deep-sea creatures as described in the passage?
options: To produce heat in cold water
To attract mates, lure prey, confuse predators, or communicate
To help them see in the dark
questions.explain: 根据文章第二段，生物发光用于吸引配偶、引诱猎物、迷惑捕食者或交流（attract mates, lure prey, confuse predators, or communicate），因此选项B正确。

questions.q: According to the passage, how do some deep-sea creatures avoid being seen by predators?
questions.explain: 第三段明确指出，许多深海生物通过透明身体（transparent bodies）来避免被捕食者发现，例如玻璃章鱼几乎完全透明。所以选C。

questions.q: What does the word "tremendous" in paragraph 4 most probably mean?
questions.explain: 第四段描述巨乌贼时用了“tremendous size”，后面提到其长度可达13米，因此“巨大”符合语境。选项C“huge”正确。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the last paragraph about the deep ocean?
options: It is fully explored by scientists.
It still holds many undiscovered species.
It is similar to the surface of Mars.
questions.explain: 最后一段提到“there are still countless wonders waiting to be discovered”，以及“we know more about the surface of Mars than about the deepest parts of our own planet”，暗示深海仍有大量未发现物种。选项C正确。
